findings.title: Materials' 59-point lens gap is extreme
findings.body: Materials sits at the 25th percentile on forward earnings but the 84th on trailing, a 59-point spread that is the widest in the table. The market is underwriting 110 percent earnings growth, which would be a historic rebound from a depressed base, not a steady-state expectation.

findings.title: Health Care's forward percentile hits 100
findings.body: Health Care's forward multiple is at the 100th percentile of its five-year range, yet its trailing percentile is only 87. That 13-point gap, combined with 88 percent implied growth, means the market is pricing in a near-doubling of earnings that has not yet appeared in reported results.

findings.title: Energy's trailing richness contradicts cheap forward
findings.body: Energy trades at the 85th percentile on trailing earnings but only the 37th on forward, a 48-point inversion. The 41 percent compression implies analysts expect a 69 percent earnings surge, yet the sector has been getting cheaper over the past month, suggesting the market is not buying the rebound.
